claim_one_line: X10 SHARPENED, NOT CLOSED. The orbit-to-point gap is NOT a gap in evidence -- it is STRUCTURAL: an orbit invariant is constant on the orbit, so it cannot pick a point, and no refinement of the SAME invariant ever will. Exactly two routes exist: SHRINK THE GROUP (Q -> Z, the arithmetic route B962 already identified as where homogeneity fails) or ADD NON-INVARIANT STRUCTURE. The concrete next computation is the count of G(Z)-orbits inside the object's G(Q)-orbit, with an honest UNFAVOURABLE prior. P0 QUANTIFIER stated before computing: this is about the ALGEBRA AND ITS ARITHMETIC (rational and integral orbits of pairs of 27s under the Kato-Yukie action), NOT a manifold -- nothing here says anything about m004, its class, its rows or its child. THE ARGUMENT: let G act on the space of pairs of 27s and let O be the G(Q)-orbit containing the the object's pair v; EVERY POINT OF O IS G(Q)-EQUIVALENT TO v BY THE DEFINITION OF AN ORBIT, and the cubic etale algebra is an ORBIT INVARIANT, constant on O -- which is precisely why it classifies orbits at all -- so NO INVARIANT BUILT FROM THE G-ACTION CAN DISTINGUISH ONE POINT OF O FROM ANOTHER, making a canonical point inside O not merely unproved but UNREACHABLE BY ANY ORBIT INVARIANT. Asking the orbit invariant to pick a point is asking a class function to pick a representative. WHAT THIS RULES OUT, worth stating because it is the tempting direction: sharpening the SAME invariant -- a finer cubic, more primes, a better splitting statistic -- CANNOT close the gap, nor can a second orbit invariant, since every such move is constant on O. ROUTE A, SHRINK THE GROUP: replace G(Q) by a subgroup not acting transitively on O, naturally the arithmetic G(Z) or G(O_K), so O breaks into finitely many integral orbits -- and this is B962's banked observation and the reason the opening was live at all, that OVER Z OR A NUMBER FIELD HOMOGENEITY FAILS; the count of G(Z)-orbits inside one G(Q)-orbit is a CLASS NUMBER-type quantity, and IF IT IS 1 the integral orbit IS a canonical point up to G(Z), which is exactly what a VEV direction needs since a VEV is only ever defined up to the unbroken group. ROUTE B, ADD NON-INVARIANT STRUCTURE: impose a condition that is NOT G-invariant -- reality/positivity, an integrality lattice, or compatibility with a second structure the object independently supplies -- breaking O by construction rather than by invariant. THE CONCRETE NEXT COMPUTATION: route A, counting the G(Z)-orbits inside the the object's G(Q)-orbit, the pair being already integral in the B854 Chevalley frame (B884: every coefficient +-1, unit structure constants inherited not chosen). HONEST PRIOR, STATED BEFORE RUNNING: UNFAVOURABLE -- class numbers of this kind are generically greater than 1 and the the programme's history is a record of homogeneity winning (B962: OP^2 = F4/Spin(9) is homogeneous, and a canonical point of a homogeneous space exists only if the space is a point); what makes it worth running anyway is that Q -> Z is PRECISELY where B962 says homogeneity fails, the one place the unfavourable prior could be wrong FOR A STATED REASON rather than by hope. THE RUNG STAYS OPEN; what changed is that it now has a NEXT STEP instead of a caveat.
